tags.label: C#
tags.summary: C# is the primary language used in Unity development. It is a statically typed, object-oriented language running on the .NET runtime.

tags.label: Unity
tags.summary: Unity is a cross-platform game engine. Scripts inherit from MonoBehaviour and interact with the engine through a defined lifecycle.

tags.label: Unity Lifecycle
tags.summary: Unity calls methods on MonoBehaviours in a defined order: Awake → OnEnable → Start → FixedUpdate → Update → LateUpdate → OnDisable → OnDestroy.

tags.label: Basics
tags.summary: Fundamental patterns and practices in Unity or C# that every developer should know before moving to advanced topics.

tags.label: Object-Oriented Programming
tags.summary: OOP organises code around objects with data and behaviour. Core pillars are encapsulation, inheritance, polymorphism, and abstraction.

tags.label: Inheritance
tags.summary: Inheritance lets a class derive from another, reusing and extending its behaviour. C# supports single class inheritance but multiple interface implementation.

tags.label: Collections
tags.summary: C# collections (List, Dictionary, HashSet, Queue, etc.) are in System.Collections.Generic. Choosing the right collection for access patterns matters for performance.

tags.label: ScriptableObjects
tags.summary: ScriptableObjects are Unity assets that store data independently of any scene. They are ideal for shared configuration, events, and decoupling systems.

tags.label: Coroutines
tags.summary: Coroutines are Unity's built-in way to spread work across multiple frames using yield. They run on the main thread and are not true multithreading.

tags.label: Async / Await
tags.summary: C# async/await enables asynchronous programming using Tasks. In Unity, UniTask is preferred over Task for performance and integration with the main thread.

tags.label: Addressables
tags.summary: Unity Addressables is an asset management system that loads assets by address (string or AssetReference) asynchronously. It replaces Resources.Load for scalable projects.

tags.label: Events & Delegates
tags.summary: Delegates are type-safe function pointers. Events wrap delegates with subscribe/unsubscribe semantics. Action and Func are built-in generic delegate types.

tags.label: LINQ
tags.summary: LINQ (Language Integrated Query) provides a fluent API for filtering, transforming, and aggregating collections. Avoid it in hot paths due to allocation overhead.

tags.label: Memory & Performance
tags.summary: C# uses a garbage collector. Frequent allocations on the heap cause GC spikes. Techniques like object pooling, structs, and Span<T> reduce GC pressure.

tags.label: Physics
tags.summary: Unity physics runs in FixedUpdate. Rigidbody controls physical simulation. Use Physics.Raycast and OverlapSphere for spatial queries.

tags.label: Design Patterns
tags.summary: Design patterns are reusable solutions to common problems. Common ones in Unity include Singleton, Observer, Command, Object Pool, and Service Locator.
